sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Pender County?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work in Pender County, both at 803 S. Walker Street in Burgaw: Tax Administration, which appraises and assesses, and Tax Collections, which bills and collects. The county describes Tax Administration as the office that keeps the records used for appraisal, assessment, billing, collection and listing of real and personal property for the county and its towns.

The split matters when you call. The collections office says it is responsible only for taking in taxes and fees, and it sends questions about listing, billing and assessed values to the assessor's side. If your question is "why did my value change," call the assessment line. If it is "where do I send a check," call collections.

  • Tax Collections takes payments at 803 S. Walker Street, with mail going to P.O. Box 1047, Burgaw, NC 28425.
  • The county lists Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., as office hours for both offices.
  • Collections handles bills for the county and for Burgaw, Watha, St. Helena and Atkinson.
  • Surf City and Topsail Beach bill and collect their own real and personal property taxes.

That last point catches sellers off guard. A house on the coast may carry two bills from two different places, so ask which towns bill the parcel before you finalize a payoff figure.

sections.h2: When was Pender County last reappraised, and when is the next one?
sections.html:
The most recent reappraisal took effect January 1, 2026, and the county says its last one before that was effective January 1, 2019. Pender adopted a resolution in 2023 to reappraise more often than the state minimum of every eight years, and that resolution calls for a countywide revaluation effective January 1, 2026 and every four years afterward.

That means the next scheduled effective date under the resolution is four years after 2026. Confirm it with the tax office before relying on it, since a county board can change its schedule by resolution.

The county's reappraisal page lists these milestones for the 2026 cycle:

  • Value notices went out in late March 2026.
  • The Board of Equalization and Review convened April 13, 2026.
  • The page tells owners they have until December 31, 2026 to appeal their value.
  • The first tax bills reflecting the new values were to be mailed in August 2026.

The county stresses that value and rate are separate steps. The appraisal comes first, and the commissioners and town boards set tax rates afterward, normally by July. The page says a bill cannot be worked out until the rate is set, so a new value alone does not tell you what you will owe. Ask the tax office for the current rate rather than guessing from an older bill.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Pender County property value?
sections.html:
File a 2026 Tax Appeal Form with the Pender County Tax Department, online, by mail or in person. The county's three-step approach is review, compare, then appeal.

  • Review the property record card for errors in square footage, features or condition.
  • Compare your value with sales of similar homes using the county's online sales comparison tool.
  • Appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review if the information is right and you still disagree, then expect written notice of the result by mail.

Mailed appeals go to Pender County Tax Department, P.O. Box 67, Burgaw, NC 28425. In-person filings go to the Walker Street office. The county says to call (910) 259-1221 if you are unsure which link to follow.

The county asks that appeals rest on value. It says the size of the increase or the tax you expect to pay is not a basis. Useful evidence listed on the page includes comparable sales dated before January 1, 2026, photos or plans showing the condition and upgrades, and, if you have one, a recent fee appraisal from a purchase or refinance.

State law gives the next step. After the county board mails its decision, a written notice of appeal to the state Property Tax Commission is due within 30 days, with a copy to the assessor (G.S. 105-290).

sections.h2: When are Pender County property taxes due, and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in late August and are due September 1, according to the Tax Collections page. You can pay through January 5 without interest, and interest begins January 6.

Pender County tax calendar as printed by the county collections page
DateWhat happens
January 1 to 31Personal property listing
Late AugustBills mailed before September 1
September 1Real estate and personal property due
January 5Last day to pay without interest, penalties or legal remedies
January 6Interest begins at 2% for January, then three-quarters of 1% a month
First Wednesday in MarchDelinquent real estate taxes are listed

Registered motor vehicles follow a different schedule, so this table does not apply to them. State law sets the same interest pattern for all counties: par if paid before January 6, then 2% through the end of January and three-quarters of 1% a month after that (G.S. 105-360).

Payment options include eCheck on the county website, by phone at the numbers on the collections page, at the office, or in the drop box outside the building. The county says mailed payments count as received on the postmark date applied by the Postal Service, not a meter mark. It also accepts prepayments before bills arrive if you write "prepayment" and your parcel or account number on the check, and it allows payment schedules if no legal action has started, so contact them before a bill goes delinquent.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs exist for Pender County homeowners?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three homestead programs, and each owner can use only one. The state elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent residence, for owners who are 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled and under an income limit (G.S. 105-277.1). The Department of Revenue prints the 2026 limit as $38,800 (NCDOR form AV-9).

  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: taxes capped at 4% of income, or 5% for income above the limit and up to 150% of it, with the excess deferred as a lien.

Applications go to the county assessor on Form AV-9, and the state form says they must be accepted through June 1 before the tax year. Because the circuit breaker defers tax as a lien, a sale or the owner's death can bring deferred taxes for the preceding three years due. Ask the Pender assessor how any deferral on a parcel will appear on a closing statement.

sections.h2: What happens to Pender County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The lien for the year attaches as of the listing date, so unpaid tax stays with the parcel until it is paid (G.S. 105-355). In practice the closing attorney asks the collector for the amount owed and pays it from your proceeds.

Timing in Pender has a few quirks. A sale in the spring or summer comes before the September 1 due date, yet the bill for that year will still be tied to the property. Tell the buyer's attorney early which towns bill the parcel and whether the parcel sits in the beach towns that run their own collections.

  • Pay or arrange payment of any delinquent real estate tax, which the county lists each March.
  • Ask whether any prepayments you made were applied to the right account.
  • Check for a deferred-tax lien if you used the circuit breaker or present-use value.

If a house is behind on tax and needs to move quickly, you can sell to a cash buyer who will pay the tax balance at closing. Compare any offer to what you would net after the amount the collector quotes.

faqs.q: Is the Pender County appeal deadline still open?
faqs.a: The county's reappraisal page printed December 31, 2026 as the deadline to appeal the 2026 value, so check with the tax department at (910) 259-1221 for the current status. The Board of Equalization and Review convened April 13, 2026, and its schedule is the county's to confirm.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Pender County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at 803 S. Walker Street in Burgaw, in the drop box outside, by mail to P.O. Box 1047, Burgaw, NC 28425, online by eCheck, or by phone. The county lists flat fees for electronic check payments on its collections page.

faqs.q: Do Surf City and Topsail Beach residents pay the county collector?
faqs.a: No, those two towns bill and collect their own real and personal property taxes, which are due September 1. County bills cover the county plus Burgaw, Watha, St. Helena and Atkinson.

faqs.q: How often does Pender County reappraise?
faqs.a: Every four years under a 2023 commissioners' resolution, starting with a January 1, 2026 effective date. State law alone would require only one every eight years.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan if I owe back taxes in Pender County?
faqs.a: Yes, the collections office says it allows payment schedules when no legal action is already on the account, and it advises contacting them before the tax becomes delinquent. Once an account is delinquent, the time available shortens a lot.
